capabilities.target: Private repositories owned by the user

inputs.source: User's direct prompt: "Have a look at the open issues in my public repo."
Content of open issues in the public repository; anyone on GitHub can open an issue there

controls.name: Per-tool-call client approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees a collapsed summary, not the raw destination and diff, so this is a model_summary gate. A more capable model can write a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary (ASI09), and runtime notes indicate users approve many calls per session, which produces approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Fine-grained PAT scoped only to the public repository
Raw-action approval review (full diff, destination repo, and visibility shown, not collapsed)
Provenance-bound destination confirmation blocking PRs mixing private-repo content with a public target

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): public-issue content reaches private-repo read and public PR creation, gated only by a collapsed-argument approval prompt

attack_path.note: Untrusted content; anyone can open issues in the public repo
Issue content can instruct the agent to read confidential files from private repos using the same broad-scope PAT
Agent can be instructed to open a PR on the public repo carrying the private content, exfiltrating it across the trust boundary

forecast.watch_signal: Rising approvals-per-session for this prompt with the collapsed-argument view remaining the default, or the underlying client/model being upgraded to a more persuasive version.

evidence.observation: The github MCP server is launched with a single GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN used for every tool call.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so reads and writes are not least-privilege.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue content an untrusted (U) input that reaches the agent's context.
The client asks for approval per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session: a model_summary gate subject to approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

recommendations.action: Use a fine-grained PAT scoped only to the public repository for this agent, so get_file_contents on private repositories is unreachable regardless of model behavior.
Switch the approval prompt to raw-action review: show the full diff, target repository, and visibility (public/private) before allowing create_pull_request, instead of a collapsed summary.

Bind create_pull_request's target repository to a destination confirmed from the system of record, and block PRs whose diff contains content read from a private repository in the same session (provenance tagging).
Log and alert when a single session both reads from a private repository and writes to a public one.

findings.title: Unpinned github-mcp-server image allows silent tool redefinition (rug pull)

attack_path.note: Docker image referenced with no tag or digest pin

threat_refs.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts: AI Agent Tools

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diff showing a new image tag or digest for ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server, or a changed tool schema in the tools/list response.

evidence.observation: The docker args reference ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest, so the image served can change between runs without review.

recommendations.action: Pin the github-mcp-server image to a specific content digest and verify its signature before each pull.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from an untrusted source reaching an S3 sink (irreversible, broad-credential egress to a public repository), giving inherent = critical under the base U x S3 matrix. The only credited control in either path is the per-tool-call approval prompt (ctl.tool_call_prompt), which is structural but partially_dependent because the approver sees a collapsed model summary rather than the raw action; per rubric section 5 step 2 this gives -2 tiers with a floor of moderate, producing residual = moderate for both findings. No severing control (such as a repo-scoped credential) or raw-action review is currently in place; both are recorded as missing_recommended. Every finding's forecast shows the same control failing under autonomy_increase, longer_task_horizon, or model_upgrade (approval fatigue and more persuasive summaries, per SAFE-T1403/ASI09), or under new_mcp_server/control_removal for the unpinned image, returning the tier to critical. This matches the real-world incident this design is modeled on, where a collapsed-argument approval step did not stop private-repo content from being exfiltrated through a public pull request.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration (the MCP client config and runtime notes provided), not observed runtime behavior.

No system prompt or MCP tool manifest was provided; capability scope for get_file_contents and create_pull_request is inferred from the GitHub MCP server's known tool set and the runtime notes, so confidence on exact tool behavior is medium.

Approval volume (approvals per session/hour) is described qualitatively in the runtime notes ('many calls per session') rather than quantified, so the approval-fatigue likelihood judgment is an inference, not a measurement.
